deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the proof of 'Proposition 2' from the previous page. The statement: if u is a compact operator on a (complex) Hilbert space E with eigenvalues (λ_i), counted with algebraic multiplicity, then the n-th exterior power Λ^n u is compact on the Hilbert exterior power Λ̄^n E. Its eigenvalues are exactly the products λ_{i1}…λ_{in} with i1<…<in.

Compactness was handled on the previous page. The map u ↦ Λ^n u is continuous and sends finite-rank operators to finite-rank operators, so Λ^n u is a norm limit of finite-rank operators.

The eigenvalue statement is first proved for u of finite rank, by reduction to linear algebra:
- Split E as an orthogonal sum E = E_0 ⊕ E_1, with E_0 finite-dimensional and carrying the non-trivial part of u.
- Use the Hilbert version of the algebra isomorphism Λ(E_0⊕E_1) ≅ Λ E_0 ⊗ Λ E_1. The prehilbertian structures are compatible, so Λ̄^n E = ⊕_{p+q=n} Λ^p E_0 ⊗ Λ̄^q E_1 is an orthogonal decomposition.
- On decomposable vectors, Λu(x_1∧…∧x_n) = ux_1∧…∧ux_n. This vanishes as soon as a factor lies in E_1, using u(E_1)=0 and u(E_0)⊂E_0 as written on the page.
- Hence Λ^n u kills every summand with q≠0 (equivalently, every summand not of the form Λ^n E_0). Its nonzero eigenvalues are therefore those of Λ^n(u|E_0) on the finite-dimensional space Λ^n E_0.

For a matrix, one shows (e.g. by triangularization) that the eigenvalues of Λ^n A are the products of n eigenvalues with distinct indices.

The general compact case presumably follows by approximation, using continuity of the nonzero spectrum and of Riesz projections. The next page treats this and then derives Corollary 2. That corollary is the Weyl-type inequality |λ_1…λ_n| ≤ ‖Λ̄^n u‖ = s_1…s_n, with ‖Λ̄^n u‖ computed via (u*u)^{1/2}.

This is the exterior-power route to Weyl's inequalities. Grothendieck used it to bound eigenvalues of nuclear and p-summing operators in 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' and 'La théorie de Fredholm'.
errors: As transcribed, the decomposition requires u(E_1)=0 and u(E_0)⊂E_0 with E_0 ⊥ E_1. For a general finite-rank operator such an orthogonal splitting need not exist: the Fitting decomposition ker u^k ⊕ im u^k is not orthogonal. The previous page's choice (E_1 = intersection of iterated images, E_0 its orthogonal complement) also does not give these properties in general.

The gap is easily repaired. Take E_0 finite-dimensional containing u(E) and E_1 = E_0^⊥. Then Λ^n u maps all of Λ̄^n E into Λ^n E_0, so its nonzero eigenvalues (with algebraic multiplicity) are those of Λ^n(u|E_0). This is a block-triangular rather than block-diagonal argument.
The passage from finite rank to compact u, with multiplicities preserved, needs upper semicontinuity of the spectrum plus continuity of Riesz projections. That step is not visible on this page.

ideas.what: Eigenvalues of Λ^n u for compact u are the products of n eigenvalues with distinct indices; Λ^n u is compact on the Hilbert exterior power.
ideas.modern_name: Spectral theory of antisymmetric tensor powers of compact operators
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Weyl (1949), A. Horn (1950); in Banach-space form Grothendieck and later Pietsch, König
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques (Mem. AMS 16, 1955), Ch. II; La théorie de Fredholm (Bull. SMF 84, 1956)

ideas.what: Orthogonal decomposition Λ̄^n(E_0⊕E_1) = ⊕ Λ^p E_0 ⊗ Λ̄^q E_1 of Hilbert exterior powers.
ideas.modern_name: Exponential property of the exterior algebra (Fock space factorization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard multilinear algebra / Fock space folklore

ideas.what: Leads to Weyl's inequality |λ_1…λ_n| ≤ s_1…s_n via ‖Λ^n u‖ (next page).
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques, Ch. II (eigenvalue estimates for nuclear/Fredholm operators)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of a standard lemma (eigenvalues of exterior powers of compact operators, en route to Weyl's inequality) that Grothendieck published in 1955–56. It contains a minor fixable gap in the choice of decomposition and nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Line 4 likely reads 'orthogonale Λ̄^{(n)}E = Σ_{p+q=n} Λ^p E_0 ⊗ Λ^{(q)} E_1' (superscript p over E_0).
The final parenthetical '... hypergéométrique [?]' is more plausibly '... matrices triangulaires' or similar (triangularization argument), not 'hypergéométrique'.
'u(E_1)=0, u(E_0)⊂E_0, dim E_0 fini' appears underlined near the middle of the page.
'Λ̄^n E_0 = Λ̄ E_0' should probably read Λ̄^n E_0, the top exterior power if n = dim E_0 is intended, or the n-th power of E_0.
